title: Interpreting Social Respect: A Normative Lens for ML Models
benchmark_measurement: Bias in a toxicity detection model, specifically measuring how the model's internal representations associate identity terms, including religious identities like 'muslim', with the concept of toxicity.
findings: The paper uses the identity term 'muslim' as an example of a marginalized group identity. While the main experimental results shown are for LGBTIQ+ identities, the findings are generalizable. The study found that a bias-mitigated toxicity model (TOXICITY@6) showed a significantly lower internal association between identity terms and toxicity for neutral and positive comments compared to an earlier version (TOXICITY@1), demonstrating that internal model representations of social values can be measured and improved.
references: L. Dixon, J. Li, J. Sorensen, N. Thain, and L. Vasserman. Measuring and mitigating unintended bias in text classification. In Proceedings of AAAI/ACM Conference on AI, Ethics, and Society, 2018.
